Staff EV Trial: “The car was a dream to drive” 
September will see the end of the 3-month Staff EV Trial for 
business travel, in partnership with the Sustainable Energy 
Authority of Ireland and Enterprise Rent a Car. The trial was a 
success with staff saying “The car was a dream to drive” and 
“Even though I had no previous experience of electric cars it was 
easy to understand and operate”.  
The car was used by staff for business travel on more than 50 
occasions for more than 2500Km of business travel. Environment, 
Planning and IT were the sections who used the car most. The 
journeys in the EV resulted in a saving of 175kg of carbon dioxide 
which is equivalent to boiling a kettle 11,666 times, or the amount 
of CO2 absorbed by 7 mature trees in a year! 
The trial was an excellent opportunity to learn more about EV’s 
and how they can play their part in reducing greenhouse gas. The 
findings and data be will be collated by the SEAI, and will also 
inform future policies in Kilkenny County Council. Talks are on-
going to see if the EV can be retained for a few more months to 
allow more staff to use it. We’ll keep you posted.

Team Up to Clean Up-Together for Kilkenny 
This year’s “Team Up to Clean Up” will take place on the weekend of 20th-22nd of September 2024. 
 
The County-Wide Clean Up initiative brought together residents, businesses, and local organizations to 
collaborate in a mass effort to enhance the cleanliness and sustainability of our County.

6 
 
The “Team Up to Clean Up” event created a sense of community ownership and pride by engaging 
participants in a variety of cleanup activities, awareness campaigns, and environmental educational 
programs. It created a sense of ownership and focus for many communities, with significant additional 
interest by many groups and individuals outside of national campaigns such as the annual National 
Spring Clean which takes place during the month of April. All cohorts of society engaged resulting in 
the “Team Up to Clean Up” exemplifying best practice in the areas of social inclusion and environment. 
Community groups, schools and residents committees can register via our online portal- 
cleanup.kilkenny.ie | Team Up To Clean Up - Together for Kilkenny 
 
 
As part of the “Team Up to Clean Up-Together for Kilkenny” campaign for 2024, there will be an opportunity 
for primary and secondary schools involved in the Green Schools Programme to register for an award 
winning composting and recycling for schools programme free of charge.  
The aim of the programme is to help schools prevent waste, improve recycling and set up, start or improve 
on-site composting systems to reduce waste, save money and combat climate change. The programme 
also helps schools improve their gardening efforts and increase biodiversity around their schools. All of 
these activities assist schools with attaining their Green School Flags and reaching their Sustainable 
Development Goals. In addition, the programme gives teachers access to a wide variety of fun, participatory 
and interactive activities for school children to learn about waste prevention, recycling, composting and 
gardening. These activities support children’s understanding of the underlying principles of ecology, biology 
and biodiversity that underpin all life on our planet. 
Each participating school will receive a €250 voucher to spend on in-school collection caddies, indoor 
recycling bins, instructional signs, a variety of composting systems, including composting bins, leaf mould 
cages and wormeries, and composting tools, including secateurs, pitch forks, compost aerators, watering 
cans, thermometers and anything that supports their respective action plans.

tackle the scourge of gum litter pollution. The initiative aims to 
educate and engage the public on the importance of proper

local authorities. Its mission is to reduce gum litter and promote 
a cleaner and more sustainable environment.

around long weekends and holiday periods.

Playing Pitches  
A maintenance plan was recently completed at our Newpark and Garringreen pitches to ensure they were 
fit-for-purpose. The Newpark soccer pitch underwent verti-drain treatment, along with the application of 
sand, seed, feed and weed control. Garringreen pitch received feed and weed treatment as well. Both 
processes have significantly improved growth and appearance. Additionally, Garringreen has seen 
renovations to the paths around its playground, enhancing accessibility and overall appearance.

Meadows – Biodiversity Management 
Species-rich meadows are crucial for biodiversity, supporting a wide range of wildlife. We are pleased to 
report that all major meadows, including Bishopsmeadow, Dukesmeadow, Glendine Wood, Melville Heights 
and the Peace Park in the City have been cut and vegetation gathered. 
In Callan, the Abbey Meadows and the Moate Field have also been cut and gathered. This important process 
is vital for the long-term maintenance and care of our meadows.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Woodstock Estate 
While the weather was not great over the summer Woodstock Gardens continued to attract high numbers 
of visitors. The marketing and promotion of the gardens was key to this success as was initiatives 
introduced, such as “Woodstock Wednesday”, whereby for the month of August Wednesday’s had free entry 
with tea and scones for €5. This proved very popular and it is hoped will lead to increased future visitor 
numbers through word of mouth on our fantastic gardens. For September, our Tea Rooms will return to 
opening weekends only. 
In the gardens, over the summer months, we added over 500 plants to the herbaceous border within the 
walled garden, ensuring it will continue to bloom with vibrant autumnal colours. The autumn tree colours will 
also be a major attraction in the coming months and O’Connell Marketing will be promoting this with an 
autumn campaign, highlighting the wonderful colours and experiences Woodstock has to offer. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Kilkenny Countryside Park 
In conjunction with our service provider, we are excited to announce the launch of our social media platforms 
for the Kilkenny Countryside Park. While the park has already proven very popular  this initiative will promote 
this fantastic amenity to a wider audience. The meadows within the park will be cut in mid-September to 
allow the pollen-rich species still in flower to continue to shine.

The Affordable Homes are generally targeted at first-time buyers (exceptions apply) who need assistance 
bridging the gap between their own available funds (including the Help to Buy scheme), the mortgage that

and their mortgage capacity.

requisite documents to complete their applications subject to them meeting the qualifying criteria.  Full 
information is available at  https://kilkennycoco.ie/affordable-homes    
It is strongly recommended applicants have Mortgage Approval in Principle prior to applying for this scheme, 
as applicants will be required to demonstrate their capacity to purchase. Only valid applications (i.e. 
applications with all required documentation submitted) will go forward for assessment. Applications which 
are incomplete or those not accompanied by the required documentation will be deemed invalid.

The Tenant (Incremental) Purchase Scheme 2016, which allows local authority tenants to buy their 
homes is being revised as of from 29th January 2024.  Changes to the scheme are as follows:

sources of income.

receipt of social housing support to be considered eligible under the scheme remains at 10 
consecutive years. However, in the case of joint tenancies only one tenant is now required 
to have been in receipt of social housing supports for 10 years.

In June and July this year, BirdWatch Ireland was

Council and the National Parks and Wildlife

are found on low-lying hills, where there is young 
or cleared forest plantation, open areas and 
bog.They arrive from Africa to spend the summer 
months here in Ireland but in very low numbers. 
They have a quite bizarre and distinctive, hypnotic 
‘churring’ song sang at night time.  To assist with

vulnerable species and asked the publics

nightjar birdsong was heard in their area.  The field 
survey deployed innovative technology to capture 
audio of night time sounds, and dawn and dusk 
chorus’s and specially designed software is 
currently

hours 
of 
recordings to determine the presence of Nightjar

species on the recorded audio.
